1: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
2: Thus the heavens and the earth, and all the host of them, were finished.
3: Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman, “Has God indeed said, ‘You shall not eat of every tree of the garden’?”
4: Now Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore [ a ] Cain, and said, “I have acquired a man from the Lord .”
5: This is the book of the genealogy of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in the likeness of God.
6: Now it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
7: Then the Lord said to Noah, “Come into the ark, you and all your household, because I have seen that you are righteous before Me in this generation.
8: Then God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the animals that were with him in the ark. And God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
9: So God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
10: Now this is the genealogy of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And sons were born to them after the flood.
11: Now the whole earth had one language and one [ a ] speech.
12: Now the Lord had said to Abram: “Get out of your country, From your family And from your father’s house, To a land that I will show you.
13: Then Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, to the [ a ] South.
14: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of [ a ] nations,
15: After these things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, [ a ] your exceedingly great reward.”
16: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. And she had an Egyptian maidservant whose name was Hagar.
17: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am [ a ] Almighty God; walk before Me and be blameless.
18: Then the Lord appeared to him by [ a ] the terebinth trees of Mamre, as he was sitting in the tent door in the heat of the day.
19: Now the two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them, and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground.
20: And Abraham journeyed from there to the South, and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur, and stayed in Gerar.
21: And the Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as He had spoken.
22: Now it came to pass after these things that God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
23: Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years; these were the years of the life of Sarah.
24: Now Abraham was old, well advanced in age; and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
25: Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
26: There was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
27: Now it came to pass, when Isaac was old and his eyes were so dim that he could not see, that he called Esau his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he answered him, “Here I am.”
28: Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and [ a ] charged him, and said to him: “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
29: So Jacob went on his journey and came to the land of the people of the East.
30: Now when Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister, and said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I die!”
31: Now Jacob heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s, and from what was our father’s he has acquired all this wealth.”
32: So Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
33: Now Jacob lifted his eyes and looked, and there, Esau was coming, and with him were four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.
34: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
35: Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there; and make an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”
36: Now this is the genealogy of Esau, who is Edom.
37: Now Jacob dwelt in the land where his father was a [ a ] stranger, in the land of Canaan.
38: It came to pass at that time that Judah departed from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite whose name was Hirah.
39: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. And Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him down there.
40: It came to pass after these things that the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
41: Then it came to pass, at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh had a dream; and behold, he stood by the river.
42: When Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
43: Now the famine was severe in the land.
44: And he commanded [ a ] the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in the mouth of his sack.
45: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all those who stood by him, and he cried out, “Make everyone go out from me!” So no one stood with him while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
46: So Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
47: Then Joseph went and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, their flocks and their herds and all that they possess, have come from the land of Canaan; and indeed they are in the land of Goshen.”
48: Now it came to pass after these things that Joseph was told, “Indeed your father is sick”; and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
49: And Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather together, that I may tell you what shall befall you in the last days:
50: Then Joseph fell on his father’s face and wept over him, and kissed him.
